note: Movement library. Stable across program revisions — program.json references these by id.

exercises.name: Seated hip flexor isometric, mid-range
exercises.setup: Sit on a chair, knee at 90 degrees.
cues: Press the thigh up into your own hands at about 60 percent effort
Keep breathing throughout the hold
Loads the flexors in the range that does not provoke you
exercises.avoid: This is NOT a straight-leg raise and NOT a hanging movement.
exercises.video_search: seated hip flexor isometric hold rehab

exercises.name: Long-lever hip flexor isometric
exercises.setup: Supine, leg extended to roughly 30 degrees of hip flexion, hold against a band or partner resistance.
cues: Longer lever means more load — only progress here once the seated version is easy and symptom-free

exercises.name: Standing banded march
cues: Knee to roughly 90 degrees only
Controlled lowering — the lowering phase is where clicking was documented

exercises.name: Adductor isometric squeeze, knees bent
exercises.setup: Supine, ball or rolled towel between the knees, knees bent to 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Adductor isometric squeeze, knees at 45 degrees
cues: Longer lever, more load

exercises.name: Copenhagen plank, short lever
cues: Knee on the bench, not the ankle
Long-lever version is a later goal, not a starting point

exercises.name: Glute bridge
cues: Ribs down
Do not arch the lower back to finish the rep — finish with the glute

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
cues: Left side first, one extra set on the left — documented left gluteus maximus deficit

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
cues: Chin tucked
Ribs down
Finish with the glute, not the lower back
exercises.rationale: Best heavy glute-max builder with essentially zero spinal shear and no lumbar extension moment. The anchor lift — progress it aggressively.

exercises.name: Dead bug, slow
cues: Lower back stays flat against the floor throughout
If it lifts, shorten the range
exercises.rationale: Anti-extension trunk work — the single most relevant home exercise for the Bertolotti segment.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.rationale: The transitional segment dislikes rotation under load. Builds tolerance for it.

exercises.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
cues: Dumbbells at your sides, or front-racked
Front foot far enough forward that the shin stays fairly vertical
Knee tracks over the toe — knee caving inward is FADIR under load
exercises.video_search: rear foot elevated split squat setup

exercises.name: Heavy sled push or drag
exercises.rationale: Near-zero spinal load, high leg force, transfers directly to running mechanics. If you only did hip thrusts and heavy sled you would still get most of the result.

exercises.name: Nordic curl (or GHR, or slider leg curl)
exercises.rationale: Posterior chain strength with no spinal load at all.

exercises.name: Front squat
cues: More upright torso, smaller lumbar extension moment than back squat
Knees out
Use lifting straps in the rack if the standard front-rack aggravates the right shoulder

exercises.name: High-bar back squat
cues: Bar sits on the traps, not the rear delts — low-bar rack position is OFF the menu due to shoulder retroversion
Upright torso, knees out, controlled descent
If the grip aggravates the right shoulder, take a wider grip or use lifting straps around the bar
exercises.rationale: Primary working squat variant. High-bar produces a more vertical torso than low-bar and a smaller lumbar extension moment — safer over a Bertolotti segment. It's also the version this user can rack given the posterior shoulder pathology.

exercises.name: Safety squat bar back squat
cues: SSB handles in front — no shoulder external rotation required to rack the bar
The camber pushes you forward, so brace hard and stay upright
exercises.rationale: The friendliest heavy squat variant for this shoulder. If the box has one, prefer SSB for the main squat slot until the shoulder is a solved problem.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat, dumbbells
cues: Dumbbells at your sides
Front shin close to vertical — knee-forward drive loads the labrum
Left side gets the extra set — documented left glute-max and left hip-flexor deficit
exercises.rationale: Heavier progression of the RFE split squat. Unilateral loading is the primary tool for closing the left-right strength gap the record documents.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
cues: Kettlebell or dumbbell in the opposite hand to the working leg
Hinge at the hip, keep the spine long, do not round the low back
Left side gets the extra set
exercises.rationale: Unilateral posterior-chain loading, teaches hip hinge with a stable spine, and closes the left glute-max gap. Non-negotiable in every training week.

exercises.name: Block pull, mid-shin height

default.setup_note: bar starts at mid-shin, ~10-15 cm elevated

cues: Shortens the range of motion, reduces the flexion demand at the pull start
Neutral spine, brace before you lift, drive with the legs
This is the primary heavy pull until conventional deadlift is symptom-free

exercises.name: Conventional deadlift from the floor
cues: Only if the block pull has been symptom-free at ~150 kg for at least 4 weeks
Brace hard, neutral spine, lats engaged, drive the floor away
Any left SI or groin symptom in the next-morning check means back to block pulls

exercises.name: Daily air-squat skill practice
cues: Bodyweight or empty bar only
Slow tempo, full depth without pain, focus on knees tracking over toes
This is technique work and joint nutrition, NOT stimulus — do not chase fatigue
exercises.rationale: Frequency practice. The research signal on daily squatting is that it produces better technique and consistency, not more hypertrophy. Treat it as skill practice.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Dumbbell or kettlebell held at the chest
Full depth without knees caving

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
cues: Heavy weight in one hand only
Stay tall, ribs down, do not lean toward the load
exercises.rationale: Anti-lateral-flexion + anti-rotation loaded carry — direct fit for the left transitional segment.

exercises.name: Farmer's carry
cues: Heavy weight in both hands
Tall posture, controlled breathing, small fast steps

exercises.name: Trap-bar deadlift from blocks
cues: Neutral grip, less shear than a straight bar

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
cues: Posterior pelvic tilt FIRST
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg
Only lean until you feel a mild stretch
exercises.warning: You should feel it in the front of the thigh, not deep in the groin or the front of the hip joint. Deep anterior hip pinching means you are loading the labrum — back off immediately.
exercises.video_search: half kneeling hip flexor stretch posterior pelvic tilt

exercises.name: 90/90 hip switches
cues: Controlled, no bouncing
Stay inside the pain-free range
Skip if it pinches

exercises.name: A-march
cues: Knee to approximately 90 degrees only

exercises.name: Controlled leg swings, front to back
cues: Small range — this is a primer, not a stretch

exercises.name: Hollow hold
exercises.notes: Substitute for GHD sit-ups and kipping toes-to-bar in class.

exercises.name: Strict knee raise to 90 degrees
cues: Stop at 90 degrees
Slow, controlled lowering
exercises.notes: Substitute for kipping toes-to-bar. Watch the shoulder as well as the hip.

class_modifications.reason: End-range lumbar extension over a pseudoarthrosis with bone oedema. Worst single movement on the list.
Doubles up: hanging loaded hip flexion (documented provocateur, with clicking) plus a hanging shoulder with a SLAP and posterior labral detachment.
Shoulder — SLAP plus posterior labrum plus spinoglenoid ganglion cyst.

class_modifications.avoid: Heavy back squat or deadlift for time
class_modifications.reason: Fatigue plus load plus lumbar flexion-extension cycling.
Lumbar extension plus overhead shoulder demand.
substitute: hang power snatch at moderate load

class_modifications.reason: Knees caving equals flexion plus adduction plus internal rotation under load — the positive test position.
class_modifications.action: Cue knees out, reduce depth when form degrades
